messages:
maya: FYI, AcmeAnalytics hit repeated 429s and token latency spikes on their Dedicated pool this morning. Customer says peak QPS briefly doubled during a marketing surge and app errors followed.

tony: saw the alert chain. autoscaler didn't kick in fast enough; pool was at 60% GPU util baseline and then jumped to ~92% for a few minutes.

ops-bot: [alert] dedicated-pool-us-east-1:acme-pool GPU util > 90% for 3m, throttles detected.

elaine: can you paste the autoscaler settings for that pool? policy + cooldown?

tony: policy: target_util=0.65, max_instances=8, min_instances=2, scale_up_cooldown=30s, scale_down_cooldown=5m. (from console)

maya: customer reports baseline QPS ~120 req/s, typical peak ~250 req/s, this incident peak ~520 req/s for ~6m. They expected Dedicated to absorb bursts.

ryan: billing-bot shows usage spike for that account at 03:12 UTC; cost alert hit but customer hasn't been billed yet due to monthly cycle. flagged.

support-tier2: quick hypothesis: pool max_instances=8 couldn't keep up with sudden doubled peak; continuous batching also saturated KV cache memory leading to longer p50/p90. Noisy neighbor? possible but util pattern aligns w/ their burst.

tony: noisy neighbor would show other model processes spiking concurrently on same nodes. looking at per-instance metrics: instance-3 and instance-4 had 99% SM utilization and high memory pressure starting 03:10. others were 70-80. Not uniform.

elaine: steps to repro (from customer): 1) use their traffic replay script replay_traffic.sh (they provided). 2) hit the pool endpoint with 520 qps sustained for 5m. They included snippet: ```bash
./replay_traffic.sh --qps 520 --duration 300 --endpoint https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate --key REDWOOD_KEY```

maya: customer says they didn't expect throttle errors until >75% util per docs. we need to check docs vs actual autoscaler target.

tony: docs say target 0.7 default for new pools but this one is 0.65. Also scale_up_cooldown=30s might be too long for sudden traffic bursts.

support-tier2: proposed immediate mitigation: increase max_instances to 16 and set target_util to 0.5 for Acme pool to aggressively scale during promo windows. Also enable burst_capacity override for 10% temporary burst.

maya: can we do that without affecting billing unexpectedly? need to notify customer before scaling to 16.

billing-bot: note: increasing max_instances will allow autoscaler to create up to 16 instances; cost will scale with instance-hours. Can set a temporary annotation to auto-revert after 8 hours.

ryan: I can message Acme to get approval for temporary scale up — queued.

tony: operational play: 1) create a canary pool with same model pinned and run traffic replay to confirm behavior; 2) adjust scaling policy on production to 16/0.5; 3) monitor prefix cache hit rate and KV pressure.

elaine: also check model parallelism settings and batch size. Their model variant is quantized; batching may be increasing latency under memory pressure. try reducing max_batch_tokens to 1024.

maya: customer also reported a spike of 504 gateway errors in their app. logs show Redwood responded slowly >30s, then 429s. Could be queue saturation + client retry storms.

tony: adding a short-term mitigation: enable 2s client-side retry-backoff doc and implement per-route rate limiter to smooth bursts (we can push a config change at infra level).

ops-bot: action created #INC-2025: Acme dedicated throttling — assigned to tony, elaine. SLA: 4h.

elaine: I'll run repro on canary at ~17:50 UTC and post results. if we see same pattern, we'll proceed with scaling policy change.

maya: Acme approved temporary scale to 16 for 6 hours. Ryan confirmed.

tony: executing policy update now: ```json
{"pool":"acme-pool","max_instances":16,"target_util":0.5,"scale_up_cooldown":"15s"}```

ops-bot: [config-change] pool acme-pool updated by tony at 03:45 UTC

elaine: canary run results: with target qps=520, we saw no 429s after scaling; p95 improved from 2.8s -> 1.1s. KV cache hit rate dropped slightly but overall throughput stable.

maya: closing loop with customer and adding recommended config to their runbook: target_util=0.5 for big promos, max_instances 16, short cooldowns, and pre-warm before expected spikes.

support-tier2: follow-ups: create a regression alert for unexpected throttle rate >0.5% for 5m, and schedule a perf clinic with Acme to tune batching and shard configs.

ryan: emailing Acme with postmortem and cost estimate for the temporary scale.

maya: thanks team. adding notes to ticket. :thumbsup:
